items.question: What columns, header names and column order does the CSV have?
items.ticket: download their requisition list (with status and fill counts) as CSV
items.chose: Writes the header "Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created" and one column per field in that order.
items.instead: Use other header labels or order, or leave out Created or Title.

items.question: In what order are the rows written?
items.chose: Sorts a copy of the input by creation time ascending, then by id as a string, and leaves the input array unchanged.
items.instead: Keep the input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: What line terminator does the CSV use, and does the last row get one?
items.chose: Ends every line, including the last, with CRLF.
items.instead: Use LF, or join lines with no trailing newline.

items.question: Does the file start with a UTF-8 byte order mark?
items.chose: Prepends a BOM character to the output.
items.instead: Emit plain text with no BOM.

items.question: What does an empty requisition list produce?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and the header row with a CRLF, and no data rows.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or throw.

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks escaped?
items.chose: Wraps a field in double quotes and doubles inner quotes when it contains a comma, quote, CR or LF (RFC 4180).
items.instead: Also neutralise leading =, +, - or @ against spreadsheet formula injection, or quote every field.

items.question: How is a missing or null title rendered?
items.chose: Writes an empty field for a null or undefined title.
items.instead: Write the text "null" or "undefined", or a placeholder such as "(untitled)".

items.question: What format is the creation time written in?
items.chose: Writes the full ISO 8601 UTC timestamp from toISOString(), with milliseconds.
items.instead: Write a date only (YYYY-MM-DD), or a local-time format.

items.question: How are status values written, and what happens with an unknown status?
items.chose: Writes the raw status string, and throws an error naming the requisition id if the status is not open, on_hold, filled or cancelled.
items.instead: Write a human-readable label such as "On hold", or pass unknown statuses through unchanged.

items.question: What happens when openings or filled is negative, fractional, NaN or infinite?
items.chose: Throws an error naming the requisition id unless the value is a whole number of at least 0.
items.instead: Write the value as it is, or clamp or skip the row.

items.question: What happens when filled is greater than openings?
items.chose: Throws an error naming the requisition id.
items.instead: Export the row as it is, or cap filled at openings.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has an invalid creation date, and does one bad row stop the whole export?
items.chose: Validates every row before building any output and throws on the first invalid row, so no partial CSV is produced.
items.instead: Skip the bad row, or write an empty date cell and carry on.
